requirements.req_text: Do the following: (a) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing farm equipment. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (b) Draw a plan showing a well-equipped farm shop. Point out the shop's mandatory safety devices and features. (c) Find all the universal warning and safety symbols on a piece of equipment and explain what they mean. (d) Describe what a safety data sheet (SDS) is and tell why it is used. Obtain the SDS for any engine coolant, oil, grease, fuel, hydraulic or transmission fluid, or other flammable or hazardous materials you use in meeting the requirements for this merit badge.

pamphlet_excerpts: Safety Data Sheet: A safety data sheet, or SDS, gives details about how to safelyhandle, use, and store a potentially hazardous material orproduct.
Information Data Sheet: The information on a data sheet is provided by themanufacturer and is meant to supplement the information listedon a product’s label.
SDSs Sections Provide: SDSs have 16 sections that provide general information about the chemical, identification, hazards, composition, safehandling practices, and emergency.
Additionally Technical: Additionally, other technical and scientific informationsuch as physical and chemical properties, exposurecontrol information, and toxicological.
step_by_step_procedure: Tractors Combined: Most tractors use combined transmission-hydraulic fluid tolubricate the power train and operate the hydraulic system.
Inany Tractor Type: Inany tractor, use the type of fluid or fluids recommended in theoperator’s manual.
Check Fluid Levels: Check fluid levels daily and maintaintheir proper levels.
Change Fluids Filters: Change fluids and filters at therecommended intervals.

pamphlet_excerpts: Join National FFA: Join the National FFA Organization, an agriculturaleducation organization designed for students.
Tractor Farm: As a tractor or farm equipmentmechanic, you will work on computer-controlled machineryand use computerized diagnostic tools.
Employers Generally Prefer: Employers generally prefer to hirepeople who have completed formal training programs aftergraduating from high school.
Large Tractor Equipment: Many of the large tractor and equipment manufacturers have trainingprograms to prepare individuals to work at their authorized dealerships.
step_by_step_procedure: Training Programsmay Hosted: These training programsmay be hosted at the dealerships or at community colleges or other technical institutes.
Graduates Programs Ready: Graduates of these programs are ready towork for specific manufacturer dealerships.
Community College Programs: Community college programs givestudents the chance to take additional coursework to earn an associate’s (two-year) degreein a technical field.
Extra Courses: The extra courses preparestudents to go beyond repair and maintenancepositions.

fields.Primary Standard: Find out about three career opportunities in farm mechanics. Pick one and find out the education, training, and experience required for this profession. Discuss this with your counselor, and explain why this profession might interest you.
fields.Field Evidence Recorded: Completed structured workbook organizer with specific examples, dates, and Farm Mechanics terminology.
fields.Safety & Verification: Reviewed against Official Scouting America Farm Mechanics Merit Badge Pamphlet (p. 72, p. 73) and verified during counselor conference.

worked_example.counselor_tip: Complete your Farm Mechanics Req 7 workbook organizer before class so we can spend our session time on active discussion and hands-on verification.
